title: Real Estate Video Ads on Facebook: How to Make Them in 2026
summary: Make real estate video ads on Facebook from one verified listing, a 9:16 cut with captions and a claim you can prove. Compare AI presenters with real creators.
body_markdown:
To make a real estate video ad with AI, pick one listing or one neighborhood, write one claim you can prove, script it in under 15 seconds and build it vertical with captions. Check every number against the listing before anything is generated. You can make the ad yourself with an AI video tool, or hand production to a done-for-you service. For agents and brokerages that want finished ads without running a production team,[Knowlify](https://knowlify.com/done-for-you) is the option we would start with.


Knowlify publishes this guide and is the service we recommend.


## Start with one listing and one claim you can prove


Pick one listing, or one neighborhood, for each ad. A three-bedroom on a named street gives a viewer a reason to stop, while a tour of "homes in our city" gives them nothing to act on. Write the question the ad answers before you write the script, such as whether a first-time buyer can afford a townhouse in one zip code.


Then list every fact the ad will state: price, square footage, year built, HOA fees, school assignment and commute time. Each one needs a source you can show a reviewer. A presenter should never say a number that is not on the listing, and an animated price chart needs the same check as a printed flyer.


## Build the ad in six steps


1. **Open with the question.** Meta's[mobile video guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/want-to-better-video-ads-for-mobile-well-show-you-how) asks for a message delivered in 15 seconds or less, with the most captivating elements first and the brand shown early. It also asks for an ad that works without sound.
2. **Choose the format.** An AI presenter suits a walkthrough told like a neighbor's tip. Animation suits a price range, a commute map or a before-and-after renovation. An AI commercial suits a polished brand or neighborhood film. Never use generated rooms, views or finishes to stand in for the real home: show the actual listing photos and footage for the property, and keep AI for the presenter, graphics and motion around them.
3. **Build vertical first.** Meta's[Reels ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) recommends 9:16 video with audio, with key messages kept inside the safe zone. For Facebook Feed, Meta's[video ad guide](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/video) lists 4:5 at 1440 x 1800 pixels.
4. **Add captions.** Reels play with sound on unless the viewer turns it off, and Meta says quality audio helps. Add captions anyway, so the story still reads with the sound off. Look at[Facebook video ad examples](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-video-ad-examples) for layout ideas before you brief the edit.
5. **Plan for the AI label.** Meta's[AI transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads made or significantly edited with its own generative tools when those tools add a photorealistic AI-generated person, and that the label sits next to Sponsored. Meta also says it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label, but the post does not say that detection is live yet.
6. **Test before you scale.** Meta's[A/B testing tool](https://www.facebook.com/business/measurement/ab-testing) can compare up to five ad variants with non-overlapping audiences. Keep the listing, offer, audience and budget the same, and change one thing, such as an AI presenter against a filmed version of the same script.


## Why Knowlify fits real estate video ads


Real estate creative goes stale quickly: every new listing, price drop and open house needs its own ad. Knowlify (YC S25) is the best fit for that pace because it delivers about 25 finished ads a week, lands the first batch on day 5 and has a person check every ad before it ships. It covers the three formats this guide describes: AI UGC presenters for neighborhood tips, 3D and character animation for price ranges and commute maps, and AI commercials for polished brand films.


You can take creative only and give the files to your own media buyer, or have Knowlify manage the Meta campaigns end to end. Pricing is a custom quote. Where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. On creative-only plans, if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund, with the terms on[the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) . The named clients on our Facebook video ad examples page are Parva and Casco, not real estate firms.


Pick another option when the ad needs a real person on camera, such as a seller or buyer testimonial. Knowlify does not supply human creators, build landing pages or run Google, TikTok, LinkedIn or YouTube ads.


## Can real estate agents use UGC videos in ads?


Yes, but UGC covers two different things. Real creator UGC uses a real person's footage, and Meta's[partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/ad-creative/partnership-ads) describes ads run from a creator's or partner's handle. An AI presenter has no handle of its own, so a partnership ad needs a real creator. Our[AI UGC guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-ugc-ads) explains where the AI format fits.


An AI presenter can still deliver a brand statement, such as how a buyer can compare two neighborhoods. It cannot deliver an invented customer story. The FTC's[testimonial guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. A line such as "I sold my condo in four days" needs a real seller and a real sale, whoever appears on camera.


If the ad needs a real person, a real-creator provider is the route.[Brighter Click's UGC agency page](https://www.brighterclick.com/ugc-agency) lists $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators, with full usage rights, as of October 2026. We found no real estate examples for that offer, so ask for samples from listing campaigns before you buy.
